extracted: The amounts, number of occasions and timing are the participants' own estimates, and the source of the LSD is not stated; the last dose was 1 to 180 days before sampling. The authors say the abnormality rate seemed unrelated to the number or size of doses, but note that the two people without raised rates reported the lowest average amount. Two men in the LSD group had Ph1-like chromosomes, which the authors link to chronic myeloid leukaemia, and three had quadriradials, which they link to inherited conditions with more cancer; no data on cancer are reported. They conclude that it is too early to assess the significance of the findings, yet describe the abnormalities as apparently induced by as few as four doses. Editors' calculation from Table 2: the self-estimated average amount ranks closely with the break rate (Spearman 0.86, n = 8), while the number of occasions (0.48), the largest amount (0.42) and the days since the last dose (−0.28) do not; with eight people, self-estimates of drugs of unknown content and four measures tried, the pattern is fragile, and it does not fit the 1971 review's statement that no positive study showed a relation with dose (Dishotsky et al., 1971, p. 433).
